chunks: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the House of God, and he walked; does it suffice him for the Hajj of Islam? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَجَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory Hajj (the first Hajj that makes one liable for future ones)

ai.seo_question: Does walking to Mecca fulfill the obligatory Hajj if one made a vow to do so?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the legal validity of a vow (nadhr) to perform Hajj on foot is confirmed as sufficient for fulfilling the obligatory Hajj. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the specific mode of travel vowed is accepted as the fulfillment of the religious duty, provided the core pillars of Hajj are observed. It underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the method of fulfilling vows when they align with obligatory acts.
